problem: RL PointNav policies trained in simulation break when deployed with real-world sensor noise and actuation noise. The standard remedy, fine-tuning the sim-trained policy directly on scarce real-world experience, is extremely sample-inefficient (hundreds of thousands of real steps).
motivation: Real-world robot data is expensive while simulators are cheap but imperfect. The paper argues that a small amount of high-fidelity real data is better spent adapting the simulator and the observations than adapting the policy directly. It also shows that navigation policies are extremely sensitive to perceptually minor noise: SPL collapses from 0.84 to 0.04 when mild RGB/depth noise is added.
key_idea: Close the sim-vs-real gap in two directions: a CycleGAN 'goggles' module maps real observations to sim-like ones at test time (real2sim), and a learned residual dynamics model makes the simulator's transitions behave like reality (sim2real), so the policy can be cheaply fine-tuned in the augmented simulator.
insight: Each direction fixes only its own gap, so both are needed. On the O+D settings (Table II rows 4/8/12), OA-only gets SPL 0.48/0.39/0.39 because it cannot handle actuation noise, and DA-only gets 0.05/0.01/0.08 because it cannot handle visual noise; combined BDA gets 0.62/0.60/0.63, within ~5% of an oracle fine-tuned on 1M target steps (0.65/0.62/0.73). Spending target data on a residual dynamics model, in the spirit of model-based RL, is far more sample-efficient than policy fine-tuning: most of the gain comes from the first ~1k target samples, and BDA reaches the same SPL with 36×/117×/32× less target data (avg 61×). The asymmetry of the design is deliberate. Observations are adapted real2sim so that a sensor change only needs OA retraining, not policy retraining. Dynamics are adapted sim2real because a simulator can be reset to a predicted state and reality cannot. A side finding: with sliding disabled, BDA underperforms the oracle in no-noise and observation-only settings (e.g., row 1 SPL 0.61 vs 0.84), because agents get stuck on obstacles; actuation noise is what normally unsticks them.
method: Base policy: DD-PPO PointNav agent (ResNet-50 visual encoder + 2-layer LSTM), trained from scratch for 100M steps on 72 Gibson scenes (quality 4+) in Habitat with no noise, on 64 V100s.

Data collection: the behavior policy π_sim is rolled out in both source and target to collect unpaired RGB-D images and target (state, action, next-state) tuples, with state = (x, y, θ); only 5k target samples are used for the main results.

Real2sim observation adaptor (OA): CycleGAN with generators G_sim: I_real→I_sim and G_real: I_sim→I_real, discriminators D_real/D_sim and cycle-consistency losses. It needs no paired data, is trained for 200 epochs and is applied only at test time as 'goggles'. This decouples sensing from acting, so a camera change only requires retraining OA.

Sim2real dynamics adaptor (DA): 3-layer MLP regressing the residual change in pose Δs = s_{t+1} − s_t from real transitions. It uses a weighted MSE with twice the weight on position versus orientation. During training the simulator state is reset from s^sim_{t+1} to the DA-predicted ŝ^real_{t+1} at every step (neural-augmented simulator / boosted-ensemble view).
Policy adaptation: π_sim is fine-tuned in the DA-augmented simulator (Sim_DA) using cheap simulated experience, then deployed with OA on its inputs (π_SimOA+DA).

Sim2Sim evaluation protocol (COVID stand-in for Sim2Real): target = Matterport-scanned 6.5m×10m lab (LAB) imported into Habitat, with 3 obstacle configurations × 5 waypoint episodes × 10 trials = 150 runs. Injected noise: Gaussian/Speckle/Poisson RGB, Redwood depth, and PyRobot/LoCoBot actuation models (Proportional, MoveBase DWA, ILQR). Episodes are limited to 200 steps and 40 collisions, sliding is off, and success means STOP within 0.2 m.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + 2-layer LSTM policy (DD-PPO, trained from scratch); CycleGAN observation adaptor; 3-layer MLP residual dynamics adaptor
setting.training_data: Gibson (72 scenes rated 4+) in Habitat, 100M DD-PPO steps without noise; plus 5k target-domain samples (unpaired RGB-D images and state-action-next-state tuples) to train OA/DA; then fine-tuning in the DA-augmented simulator. Sample-efficiency study uses 100/250/500/1k/5k target samples.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (LoCoBot D435-matched, 70° FOV, depth clipped at 10 m, 640×360) + GPS+Compass
setting.action_space: discrete: FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN-LEFT 30° / TURN-RIGHT 30° / STOP (stochastic under target actuation noise)
setting.simulator: Habitat (Sim2Sim: noise-free Gibson source → noisy virtualized LAB target)
setting.privileged: accurate GPS+Compass localization (standard PointNav; justified by ~7 cm Hector SLAM error on the real robot); otherwise none

numbers_note: All results are Sim2Sim, not a standard benchmark split: a Matterport-scanned lab (LAB) in Habitat with 150 runs per setting. Success/SPL are printed as fractions (0-1) and converted to 0-100 here. The sim2real-gap study (Fig. 4) is given only as a figure; the text quotes the zero-shot π100M no-noise policy at SPL 0.84 (no noise), 0.56 (D), 0.04 (O) and 0.06 (O+D). Sample-efficiency curves (100–5k target samples vs. fine-tuning) are figure-only (Fig. 7); the text states 36×/117×/32× data reductions (avg 61×), 5k samples ≈ 7 h vs ≈585k steps ≈ 836 h. OA quality is reported via FID: real vs sim 100.74 → 83.05 after OA; Gaussian-noised vs clean 98.73 → 88.44. There are no real-robot navigation results.
results: On the three observation+dynamics-noise target settings, BDA with only 5k target samples reaches SR 1.00/0.99/0.99 and SPL 0.62/0.60/0.63. This is within ~5% of an oracle fine-tuned on 1M target steps (SPL 0.65/0.62/0.73), whereas the unadapted Gibson policy scores SPL 0.11/0.03/0.05. BDA matches direct fine-tuning with 36×, 117× and 32× less target data (avg 61×); 5k samples (~7 h of robot time) match ~585k fine-tuning steps (~836 h). OA alone raises SPL under observation noise by 65% on average, and DA alone improves the D-only settings by 15% success / 11% SPL.
limitations: Real-world transfer is only simulated (Sim2Sim with hand-designed RGB/Redwood/PyRobot noise models, due to COVID). Real LoCoBot data was used only to sanity-check OA (FID) and DA (actuation error magnitudes); there is no real-robot navigation evaluation.

The test environment is a single small lab (3 obstacle configurations, 5 episodes each). BDA must be retrained per target noise setting and underperforms the oracle in noise-free and observation-only conditions (e.g., SPL 0.61 vs 0.84 with no noise), attributed to getting stuck with sliding disabled.

The DA only models a 2D pose residual (x, y, θ) for a wheeled base under discrete actions, and the task is PointNav with perfect GPS+Compass; it is unclear how this scales to richer dynamics or tasks.
